reason: Regular people (עם הארץ) are portrayed as victims of judgment and suffering throughout this passage. They experience siege and famine ('וְלֹא־ הָ֥יָה לֶ֖חֶם לְעַ֥ם הָאָֽרֶץ'), destruction of their city and temple, exile from their homeland, and those remaining are left as 'the poorest of the land' (מִדַּלַּ֣ת הָאָ֔רֶץ) to work as vinedressers and farmers. While Gedaliah briefly offers reassurance to remaining leaders, the overall arc is one of divine judgment resulting in loss, exile, fear, and displacement. The people ultimately rise up in fear and flee to Egypt.
